title: Make the writer's choices do the work.
dek: In the opening section of Robert McKee's Part IV, The Writer at Work, disciplined storytelling turns intuition into deliberate choices about structure, character, and scenes. The writer's task is to make every decision create movement the audience can feel.

marginNote.label: Apprenticeship Note
marginNote.body: A strong idea becomes a story through choices that create pressure, change, and consequence. Make the next move necessary before polishing the surface.

canon.heading: Turn intuition into choices the audience can feel.
canon.standfirst: Read the opening section of Chapter 15, "The Writer at Work," from Robert McKee's Story on PDF pages 344-368. Study how disciplined choices give an idea structure, pressure, and consequence, then stop at PDF page 368.
canon.readerIntro: Read this section as a practical test of creative decision-making. Mark where an intuitive idea becomes a choice about desire, conflict, structure, or sequence, and note what changes because of that choice. Then audit one piece of work by finding the move that creates the next necessary move. Stop at PDF page 368.

blocks.label: 01 / The writer turns instinct into design
paragraphs: An idea is only a beginning. The writer gives it force by choosing what the audience will know, want, fear, and discover next.
As you read, distinguish the initial intuition from the decisions that make it dramatic rather than merely interesting.

blocks.label: 02 / Every choice should create movement
paragraphs: A scene, character action, or structural turn earns its place when it changes the situation and narrows or reshapes what can happen next.
Look for choices that create consequence. If nothing becomes more difficult, more valuable, or newly possible, the material may be description rather than story.

blocks.label: 03 / Constraints sharpen invention
paragraphs: Creative discipline is not the enemy of originality. Limits force the writer to find the particular action, image, or sequence that carries the idea with precision.
Apply the same test to a brand or product narrative: what constraint makes the promise more specific instead of merely more elaborate?

blocks.label: 04 / Revise for necessity
paragraphs: Revision is the search for causal strength. Remove a choice and ask whether the following event still has a reason to occur; if it does, the earlier move may not be doing enough work.
Mark the point where the reading turns craft into a repeatable diagnostic rather than a mysterious talent.

blocks.label: 05 / Audit one live piece of work
paragraphs: Choose a page, pitch, campaign, or product story. Name its central desire, the pressure opposing it, and the choice that changes the audience's understanding.
Stop with one revision that makes the next move necessary. Do not add explanation where a stronger choice would create the meaning.

closeReading: Where does McKee distinguish a promising idea from the choices required to turn it into a story?
Which choice in the reading creates the clearest change in what can happen next?
What constraint makes the writer's invention more precise rather than less free?
Choose one piece of work. What does its protagonist want, what pressure resists that desire, and what choice changes the situation?
What can you remove or revise so the next move becomes necessary instead of merely available?

principle.heading: Make each creative choice carry consequence.
principle.body: A story becomes persuasive when its choices alter the field of possibility. Give the audience a desire, a pressure, and a decision whose result makes the next move feel earned.
principle.example: Instead of saying that a product helps a team collaborate, show a project lead choosing to expose a blocked dependency before a launch review; the choice creates risk, reveals the value, and makes the team's next action necessary.
principle.practice: Take one page, pitch, or campaign sequence. List its current desire, pressure, choice, and consequence. Remove one decorative move and replace it with a decision that changes what the audience expects next.

output.heading: Let the next move prove the idea.
output.body: Turn one intuition into a sequence of choices whose pressure and consequence make the audience understand why the story has to continue.

fieldNotes.title: Personal agents are being sold as follow-through, not just answers
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full for personal and professional agentic tasks, emphasizing Active Memory and Active Focus so an agent can retain relevant context, try alternate approaches, recover from errors, and ask before important actions.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The product story is moving from fluent response to accountable follow-through. The value is not that an agent can act once, but that it can keep a goal intact across difficulty without silently taking control.
fieldNotes.watch: For an agentic promise, specify the task that must be completed, the recovery behavior when it fails, and the checkpoint that keeps the user in charge.

fieldNotes.title: Away turned a viral failure into a product proof point
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Adweek reports that Away made DJ John Summit its Chief Destruction Officer after a viral video of him burning a Rimowa suitcase following repeated breakage; the partnership puts Away luggage through deliberately extreme tests.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The brand did not merely borrow attention from a viral moment. It created a new scene in which the product promise—durability—could be tested in public, giving the audience a reason to keep watching and a concrete claim to remember.
fieldNotes.watch: Look for the product or service proof that can turn a borrowed cultural moment into a designed experience with a clear consequence.

fieldNotes.title: Holiday spending is growing, but inflation is doing part of the work
fieldNotes.whatHappened: The Associated Press reports that the National Retail Federation forecasts $1.01 trillion in U.S. holiday spending for November and December, up 4.2% year over year, while economists expect higher prices to account for about half of the increase and higher-income shoppers to drive much of the spending.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: A larger market number can hide a thinner customer reality. The useful story is not simply that demand is healthy, but which shoppers can absorb price increases and which are editing the occasion around value.
fieldNotes.watch: Separate nominal growth from real demand before choosing a holiday promise; specify the customer, the pressure, and the trade-off the offer removes.

fieldNotes.title: Google is turning the shopping cart into a decision assistant
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Google launched Universal Cart in the U.S. across Search and the Gemini app, combining products from multiple retailers, price-drop tracking, promo-code discovery, payment-method suggestions, and checkout or handoff to the merchant.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: Commerce is becoming a sequence of small decisions delegated to the interface: collect, compare, watch price, and choose how to pay. The product earns trust by making each next move legible and useful rather than hiding the transaction behind automation.
fieldNotes.watch: When designing a commerce assistant, map the user's decision points and show where automation saves effort, where it makes a recommendation, and where the customer must still choose.

tweets.title: A product fragment on turning capability into behavior
tweets.summary: This fragment is useful because it names the behavioral question behind a new capability. The important test is not whether the feature is impressive, but whether it changes a repeated workflow enough for the user to adopt it.
